🖥 Trump recognized Resistance Front in MoU signed with Iran: Ghalibaf

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf says US President Donald Trump had given the US recognition to the Axis of Resistance by signing the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) that included an end to war on all fronts, including Lebanon.

In a meeting with a group of cultural elites in Tehran on Saturday, Ghalibaf referred to the process of negotiations within the US and how Trump backed down on Iran's opening of the Strait of Hormuz at the time of signing the Pakistan-brokered MoU with Tehran.
​
According to him, the US president, based on the original 15-point document, insisted that Iran must set aside its missile program, nuclear program, resistance, and the Strait of Hormuz, but he actually signed the recognition of the Resistance Front in Persian.
​
The Parliament speaker also shared the reason behind Iran's halting of the ceasefire talks with the United States, blaming it on the continued Israeli attacks on Lebanon in breach of the understanding then reached between Washington and Tehran.
​
He said Iran stopped the negotiations when the last attack by the Zionist regime on Dahiyeh resulted in the martyrdom of the head of the intelligence of the Hezbollah resistance movement and his family, adding that the Islamic Republic threatened to retaliate and target the entire region if Israel repeated its military mischief.
​
Ghalibaf also explained the US violation of the clause on lifting the blockade on Iranian ports, saying Trump's post linking the blockade to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz prompted Tehran to issue a warning to rectify such a claim since Iranians had agreed to nothing of that sort.
​
Pointing to Trump's repeated tweets and claims on the Strait of Hormuz, the top parliamentarian described the negotiations with the US as a type of combat diplomacy.

🇮🇷 Iran's Armed Forces General Staff has sent an official letter to International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) President Mirjana Spoljaric Egger regarding three Iranian Air Force pilots being held by Qatar since March.

According to the letter, signed by the commander of the Missing in Action Search Committee of Iran's Armed Forces General Staff, Sepah Pasdaran Colonel Seyed Mohammad Baqerzadeh, following the start of unlawful terrorist attacks by US armed forces and the illegitimate, usurping Zionist regime against Iran on February 28, 2026, the Iranian Air Force responded on the basis of defending national territory. On March 2, 2026, two Su-24 fighter jets departed on a combat mission toward an enemy military base stationed in Qatar. Despite achieving their initial objectives, the aircraft came under enemy air defense fire while returning and the pilots were forced to eject.

Of the four pilots involved in the mission, one, identified as Majid Kazemi, was killed. His body was returned and buried with a funeral procession in Iran.

The letter states that the three surviving pilots, identified as Javad Salehi, Abdolmajid Dashtian, and Emran Beh Roshan, were captured alive by Qatari forces. It states that despite six months having passed since Qatar's government committed to their release, Doha has, in violation of international law including the four Geneva Conventions on prisoners of war, denied the pilots their basic rights. The letter states that despite diplomatic efforts, Qatar has not permitted visits, interviews, or contact between the pilots and their families or Iranian officials pursuing the case.

The letter cites provisions of the Third Geneva Convention stating that prisoners of war must be permitted to notify their families and the ICRC of their capture, that prisoners have the right to lodge complaints with detaining authorities and to meet with protecting power representatives including the ICRC either directly or through delegates, and that severely wounded or sick prisoners, per medical assessment, are to be repatriated directly to their home country.

The letter concludes with a formal request that the ICRC president, within the framework of bilateral humanitarian cooperation, urgently arrange an interview with the Iranian pilots held in Qatar, inform Iran of their health and detention conditions, and facilitate the swift release of the men.

🖥 Iran proposes Caspian Sea consortium to monitor falling water levels

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Head of the Ports and Maritime Organization of the Islamic Republic, Mohammad Shakibi-Nasab, says Iran has proposed forming a consortium of Caspian Sea littoral states to jointly monitor the significant decline in the sea’s water level.

Shakibi-Nasab said the issue is being pursued through economic diplomacy in cooperation with the Iranian Foreign Ministry, while the Ports and Maritime Organization is providing technical support and maintaining separate contacts with Caspian littoral states.
​
He said the falling water level has become a major concern for maritime transport and could develop into a serious new challenge for the Caspian Sea.
​
In this regard, Shakibi-Nasab said Iran has proposed that countries with ports on the Caspian Sea and those using its maritime transport capacity establish a joint specialized working group to coordinate monitoring of the trend.
​
He said the proposal has been submitted to the Foreign Ministry, adding that the organization is also pursuing the issue directly with the littoral states.
​
Meanwhile, Shakibi-Nasab said the decline in the Caspian Sea’s water level is not limited to Iran and affects all countries along the sea.
​
He said coordination with Caspian countries is underway and that the United Nations is also independently following the issue.
​
On operational measures, Shakibi-Nasab identified dredging at ports as one of the necessary steps amid the falling water level and said alternative plans and joint measures may also be needed among countries using the maritime route.
​
Russia, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan are among the Caspian countries with ports that use the sea’s maritime capacity, he said.
​
However, Shakibi-Nasab said regional cooperation has not yet fully met expectations in practical and operational terms, despite countries expressing willingness to cooperate during negotiations.
​
He said efforts are continuing because a lack of cooperation would also seriously affect the maritime businesses and transport systems of the other Caspian states.
​
Shakibi-Nasab also highlighted the importance of cooperation with Russia, saying more than 80% of Iran’s maritime exchanges through its northern ports are currently conducted via Russian ports.
​
He said the scale of these exchanges requires Iran and Russia to pursue joint plans and cooperation, warning that Russian ports would also suffer significant damage if the issue is not addressed.
